title: Attorney General of Ohio

context.text: The Republican primary was uncontested: Keith Faber was the only Republican on the May 5, 2026 ballot (698,856 votes). In the Democratic primary John Kulewicz defeated Elliot Forhan, 63.1% to 36.9%.
Incumbent Attorney General Dave Yost, a Republican, resigned in May 2026 before the end of his term, so the winner will be the first newly elected occupant of the office since 2018.

candidates.name: Keith Faber
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary.

summary.text: Keith Faber is the Republican nominee. He is the current Ohio Auditor of State, a former president of the Ohio Senate (2013-2017) and a former member of the Ohio House, and an attorney from Celina. His campaign highlights his auditor's office's criminal investigations of public officials, and he says he would create an Attorney General's division of health-insurance lawyers to help consumers with denied claims.

background.text: Bachelor's degree in public administration and policy from Oakland University (1988) and law degree from the Ohio State University Moritz College of Law (1991); founder of Faber and Associates, a civil litigation and mediation firm in Celina.
Served in the Ohio House of Representatives (2001-2006 and 2017-2018) and the Ohio Senate (2007-2016), including as Senate president from 2013 to 2017.
First elected Ohio Auditor of State on November 6, 2018, and took office January 11, 2019.

priorities.text: Defend the Ohio Constitution, protect religious liberty, and defend Ohio against what his campaign calls federal overreach.
Combat the drug epidemic through addiction treatment, prosecuting suppliers and supporting recovery efforts.
Consumer protection, including a division of the Attorney General's office staffed with health-insurance (ERISA) lawyers to help consumers resolve denied claims.
Stop human trafficking and expand services for survivors.

statements.quote: And I’m a pro-life guy. But I think the voters spoke on that. And until the constitution is amended, it’s going to stop a lot of what you can do.
statements.context: In an interview with Signal Ohio, asked whether Ohio's six-week abortion ban violates the 2023 reproductive freedom amendment

statements.quote: preserve the Second Amendment rights of Ohioans
statements.context: On his campaign site's "Meet Keith" page

record.text: As Auditor of State, announced on October 8, 2026 that a Jefferson County grand jury had indicted three individuals in the alleged theft of about $20 million from the now-defunct Eastern Gateway Community College, following an investigation by his office.

As Auditor of State, announced on September 16, 2026 that a former Scioto County commissioner was sentenced to 30 months in prison after admitting involvement in a kickback scheme involving the Southern Ohio Port Authority, a case developed by the Auditor's Special Investigations Unit.

His campaign states that his office's law enforcement team has produced 170 convictions on more than 391 criminal charges against public officials since 2019 and that his team identified about $6.9 billion in unemployment compensation fraud and overpayments during the COVID-19 pandemic (campaign figures; not independently verified here).

candidates.name: John Kulewicz
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Elliot Forhan in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary.
candidates.currentRole: Member, Upper Arlington City Council (since 2020); attorney

summary.text: John Kulewicz is the Democratic nominee. He is a Columbus attorney who spent more than four decades as a litigator at Vorys, Sater, Seymour and Pease and has served on the Upper Arlington City Council since 2020. He says he would focus the Attorney General's office on consumer fraud, price-fixing and public corruption rather than what he calls culture-war cases.

background.text: Bachelor's degree in American history from the Ohio State University and law degree from Yale Law School.
Clerked for a federal judge for one year, then worked as a litigator in Columbus for over 40 years, including cases before the U.S. Supreme Court and the Ohio Supreme Court.
Elected to the Upper Arlington City Council in 2020; former president of the Columbus Chapter of the Federal Bar Association.

priorities.text: Take on corrupt politicians and restore transparency and accountability to government.
Take on price-fixing monopolies, scam artists and robocallers, and Medicaid provider and nursing-home fraud.
Move the office's resources away from what he calls culture-war cases toward consumer fraud, waste, theft and monopoly pricing.

statements.quote: With the constitution as my client.
statements.context: Asked by Signal Ohio how he would approach defending Ohio's abortion laws as Attorney General

researchNotes: Slate: the Ohio Secretary of State's certified candidate list could not be loaded (the site returned a bot-check/403), so the two-candidate slate rests on Ballotpedia and Signal Ohio's October 7, 2026 report; Ballotpedia notes its list 'may not be complete'. No independent or third-party AG candidate was found. Neither candidate has held the office, so no record items for Kulewicz (a city councilor; no council votes were reviewed). Faber's campaign conviction/finding counts are campaign claims, cited as such. Neither candidate's positions map directly onto the fixed issue statements, so only verbatim statements are shown.
